workLog.task: Verify that #3362 was superseded before reworking it
workLog.outcome: PR #3359 landed the atomic write on 2026-07-26 and closed #3357, the issue PR #3362 targeted, so #3362 was a competing implementation of a shipped fix. Diffed the two rather than assuming the merged one was complete. Main is ahead on the exit-code contract: it separates exit 3 (filesystem refused the write) from exit 1 (malformed input) per ADR-035, and preserves the primary error when close() itself fails. The branch was ahead on two things main lacks, so those became #3368 instead of a rewrite of #3362.
workLog.evidence: gh issue view 3357 reports CLOSED; gh pr view 3359 --json closingIssuesReferences returns 3357. git log on scripts/validation/merge_causal_graph.py shows 3d1f3b30d2 'write causal graph merges atomically (#3359)'.

workLog.task: Measure the temporary-file leak before fixing it
workLog.outcome: Confirmed the leak is real, not theoretical. Cleanup in _atomic_write_text is attached to except OSError. KeyboardInterrupt is not an OSError, and a merge driver runs inside an interactive git merge, which is exactly where Ctrl-C lands. The destination survives; the temporary does not get removed, and tempfile.mkstemp's default name carries no link to what wrote it, so a leaked file in .agents/memory/causality/ is unattributable and one git add -A from being committed.
workLog.evidence: Probe against origin/main at 3d1f3b30d2, forcing a BaseException out of the write: 'main leaks on BaseException: [tmpzh8km2lu.tmp]' with 'destination intact: {"a":1}'.

workLog.outcome: Added an except BaseException handler that discards the temporary and re-raises, so an interrupt cleans up. Added handle.flush() and os.fsync(handle.fileno()) before the chmod and rename, because os.replace is atomic against other processes but not against a crash: without the sync a power loss after the rename can leave the destination naming data that never reached disk, which is the partial-file outcome #3359 set out to prevent, relocated from the write to the rename. Gave mkstemp a prefix derived from the destination name so any leak is greppable. Extracted _discard() so both handlers share one unlink and neither replaces the primary error with a cleanup error.

Three negative controls, each reverting one change: dropping the BaseException handler turns 2 red, dropping the fsync turns 2 red, dropping the mkstemp prefix turns 1 red; restoring returns 73 passed. ruff check and ruff format clean on both files.
